body.statement: There is an algorithm which, from \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), outputs a finite rational class \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\), one common core radius, a common recession fan refining every nonempty component \(P_{v,b}\) with all incidence maps and semantic projections, rational chart meshes, rational partitions of unity, and a computable number \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\downarrow0\) such that for every \(K\in\mathcal C_{\eta}\) there exists \(\widetilde K_m\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\) whose semantic-label coverage is at least \(1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\), whose separated risk is at most \(R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\), and whose complete weighted ledger satisfies \(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)\).
body.justification: The global kernel is now constructive: finite active-set geometry supplies safe tail sectors, and a single shared-trace extension yields an explicit vanishing rational modulus.
body.gap: Closed by the kernel-stratified safe-sector certificate and exact shared-trace slow-collar construction; no invariant mean or equality of independently averaged charts is used.
body.consumer: The proved modulus discharges the effective-density premise used by CertGluePFL termination and replayable Gaussian certification.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: an explicit diagonal schedule over the safe shared-trace finite classes.}

Let \(A_{\mathfrak G}\) be the computable integer supplied by
\(\mathrm{lem:shared\mbox{-}extension\mbox{-}coverage\mbox{-}risk}\).  The validated finite encoding of \(\mathfrak G\) permits exact comparison with its strictly positive honesty level \(\eta\).  Therefore the search
\[
 j_0=\min\left\{j\ge2:
 j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G},\quad
 \frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}+\frac1j<1\right\}
\tag{30}
\]
terminates.  For \(m\in\mathbb N\), put
\[
 j(m)=j_0+m+1,
 \qquad
 \Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)
 =\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j(m)^2}+\frac1{j(m)}.
\tag{31}
\]
This is a positive rational number computed from the input, it decreases with \(m\), and it converges to zero.

Run the finite construction in the shared-extension lemma at level \(j(m)\), and mix every enumerated rational vertex rule globally with the full-set action using probability \(1/j(m)\).  Call the resulting finite rational class \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\).  Its geometry is computed by
\(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) on the explicit common fan \(\operatorname{recFan}(\mathfrak G)\).  Take the maximum of the finitely many chart thresholds and collar endpoints as the one common rational core radius.  The construction in
\(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) supplies the rational partitions, the global common-face mesh, all incidence maps, and the retained component-to-semantic-label projections.  Every step is a finite enumeration of rational active sets, cones, simplices, probability grids, or outward rational error allocations, so this is an algorithm from \((\mathfrak G,m)\).

Now fix \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\).  The existential nearest rational assignment in the shared-extension lemma gives \(Q_{j(m)}\) in the unrepaired finite class.  Since \(j(m)\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), its rational full-set mixture \(\widetilde K_m=Q_{j(m)}^{\mathrm{rep}}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\).  Equation (28) gives the stronger conclusion
\[
 \inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}
 P_h\{v\in\widetilde K_m(W)\}\ge1-\eta.
\tag{32}
\]
Equation (29) and (31) give
\[
 R_r(\widetilde K_m)
 \le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m),
\tag{33}
\]
and the repaired ledger conclusion of that lemma gives
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}(\widetilde K_m)
 \le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)<1.
\tag{34}
\]
The path part of (34) is legitimate even at seam-centered means by
\(\mathrm{lem:slow\mbox{-}collar\mbox{-}ledger}\) and the declared weighted-gluing inequality; it does not identify independently averaged face and cone rules.  The cone-interior products are path-independent by the declared common-ray coherence lemma, while their statistical validity follows separately from the safe-sector inclusions and (22).  Thus (32)--(34) establish every assertion in the target theorem, with the explicit input-dependent modulus (31).
